lessons: Victim of Night p1p1 and Bloodline Keeper p3p1 were taken, then cut from a WR that never splashed; commit to two colours by mid pack 1 and stop taking off-colour bombs.
The guide's WR 52% figure didn't hold: my 0-3 WR had only two Voiceless Spirits and Midnight Haunting as fliers, and Smite the Monstrous was dead against UG's Stitched Drake and Moon Heron.
Five removal spells were not enough: my 1-6 WR filled slots with two Village Ironsmiths and two Selfless Cathars; take a third flier over those ground bodies.

Don't spend early picks on weak 1-drops: I took Brain Weevil twice and Typhoid Rats and Walking Corpse, then still played all three despite planning to cut them; take cheap removal or two-drops instead.

Draft more removal that answers fliers: my deck had just four answers (Harvest Pyre, Corpse Lunge, Night Terrors, Geistcatcher's Rig) against Voiceless Spirit, Vampire Interloper, Chapel Geist and Screeching Bat.
A bomb like Olivia Voldaren doesn't carry a 17-land midrange deck alone: I went 3-5 in games with her, so value playable 2-drops and removal after the first pick.
Commit to white by pick six: my early Sensory Deprivation and Brimstone Volley went unused, and my GW deck had only one real flier, Chapel Geist, in its 1-2 loss to BG.
The guide's flier advice held: my 11-to-19-turn grinds lacked closers, so take evasive two-drops like Orchard Spirit over Thraben Sentry or a second Woodland Sleuth.
Take Thraben Sentry and Woodland Sleuth only as late filler; I spent mid-pack picks on Moorland Haunt and Murder of Crows, then played neither.
Keep on-colour reach over marginal creatures: I cut Spidery Grasp for filler, then lost 0-2 to UR's fliers (Balefire Dragon, Stitched Drake) in games of 24 and 28 turns.
Draft evasive finishers over a third cheap body: my BG midrange won 13- to 19-turn games but stalled against UR's grinding 24- and 28-turn games.
Do not first-pick off-colour removal: my pack 1 first pick, Sever the Bloodline, never reached my WG main deck and sat in the sideboard until game 2 against WB.
Tonight's Round 2 UG losses ended at 22, 19 and 11 turns, contradicting the guide's 15-to-47-turn expectation; with only Abbey Griffin and two Somberwald Spiders as fliers, take a third flier.
Contradicting the guide's 10-source rule, my 9 Forest/8 Plains WG went 1-2; give the main colour 10 sources and count Avacyn's Pilgrim as fixing.
Take Geistflame, Claustrophobia, Grasp of Phantoms and Devil's Play early: cheap removal plus 15 creatures carried U/R to 3-0 in matches, and I cut 6-drops like Geistcatcher's Rig and Rage Thrower.
Keep the curve low with cheap fliers like Stitched Drake, and cut filler like Rolling Temblor and Traitorous Blood rather than forcing them into the main deck.
I drafted without a guide, so nothing here contradicted one; my U/R plan went 3-0 in matches, but a single 6-2 game record is a small sample.
The 3-0 UR deck that beat me in round 2 ran Balefire Dragon, Devil's Play and two Geistflame; take those reach and bomb cards over mid-pack white or black filler.
The guide says fliers win, but round 3's WG deck (lost 0-2) ran two Somberwald Spider with reach, which walled my air plan; keep Rebuke or Slayer of the Wicked for reach blockers.
Prioritise blue's removal auras like Claustrophobia and Sensory Deprivation over Curse of the Bloody Tome, which I took twice in pack 1 and cut both times.
Late-pack picks went to dead cards: two Curse of the Bloody Tome, Mulch, and Fortress Crab, so take playable bodies over them when the pick is marginal.
Green 4-drops like Festerhide Boar and Boneyard Wurm plus Moldgraf Monstrosity carried my deck, but my 4-3 game record suggests securing cheap early plays before taking more top end.
